text:
South Korea proposed to hold military talks with North Korea to prevent accidental clashes stemming from unclear border lines in the Military Demarcation Line (MDL), Friday.
The suggestion comes after tensions along the border have been escalating after South Korean soldiers’ injuries from North Korean mine explosion south of the MDL amid the North’s so-called border fortification works.
“South Korea's defense ministry is formally proposing official military talks with North Korea. Seoul aims to verify the precise location of the land border, restore military hotlines, and discuss measures to prevent accidental clashes in border areas,” Kim Hong-chul, director general for defense policy at the Ministry of National Defense, said in a statement.
“The United Nations Command (UNC) can also join the discussion if necessary with specific dates and venues to be arranged through Panmunjeom.”
The announcement came about a month after three South Korean soldiers were injured by the landmine explosion while clearing a patrol route south of the MDL within the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ).
The South Korean defense ministry concluded that it was caused by the North’s landmine and the UNC confirmed it as a violation of the armistice agreement. The South has since demanded an apology from the North, which has denied responsibility for the explosion. In a related move, South Korea has sent a letter to the president of the U.N. Security Council (UNSC) on Thursday over last month's land mine explosion incident.
The remarks also came as Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, has been saying through the North’s official statements this week that Pyongyang will resume propaganda loudspeaker broadcasts against South Korea, claiming that Seoul wrongfully accused North Korean troops of crossing the border.
